title: The Measured Hand
subtitle: Tools that taught a town to make
summary: A survey of measuring tools from Rookwater workshops: rules, gauges, calipers and the chalk lines that marked every cut.
body:
The Measured Hand fills Tool Hall with cases of rules and gauges, and a chalk-line demonstration every Saturday at 2 pm.

Every object has a wall label with its accession number. The loan crates at the end of the hall travel to schools.
wall_text: Before a cut, someone measured. These tools taught Rookwater apprentices how far, how square, and when to stop.

title: Warp and Weather
subtitle: Cloth from the riverside mills
summary: Pattern books, dyed skeins and a working loom that shows how Rookwater cloth was made for the river trade.
body: Warp and Weather is the Textile Wing's permanent display. Thursday weaving demos use the floor loom by the window.
wall_text: Cloth from Rookwater's sheds traveled downriver packed in oilcloth. The patterns stayed here.

title: Fire in the Court
subtitle: Kilns, molds and Rookwater stoneware
summary: Cutaway kiln models, plaster molds and the stoneware jugs that carried vinegar and oil on the barge trade.
body: Ceramic Court is open whenever the museum is. School groups sit on the low wall for a twenty-minute clay talk.
wall_text: Heat, clay and a mold. The court shows how a jug left Rookwater and came back as a story.

title: Open Bench
subtitle: Living makers in the Workshop Gallery
summary: Three Rookwater makers install their benches for a season: a chairmaker, a pattern cutter and a blacksmith.
body: Open Bench puts unfinished work on view. Visitors watch from the rail; the makers work Thursday through Saturday.
wall_text: A bench is a sentence that is still being written. These three are writing in public.

title: School of the Hand
subtitle: How apprentices learned in Rookwater
summary: An upcoming show on apprenticeship ledgers, practice pieces and the first tools a student was allowed to own.
body: Cases are being built in the Workshop Gallery. Member previews begin March 28.
wall_text: Apprentices kept ledgers. Practice pieces were signed and dated. The first owned tool was a rite.

title: River Packing
subtitle: How goods left Rookwater
summary: A closed loan show on crates, stamps and the river packing houses. Wall text remains in the archive packets.
body: The crates returned to the lending museum. Photographs and the packing checklist stay in the Study Vault.
wall_text: Every jug, bolt of cloth and tool kit left town in a marked crate.
